faq.q: What letter styles can it generate?
faq.a: Nine structures, each with its own opening and closing wording: formal traditional, modern concise, career change, fresher/no experience, internship, referral-based, speculative/cold application, Indian government job (which uses Respected Sir/Madam and 'Yours faithfully'), and academic/research. You also set tone (formal, confident, enthusiastic, warm), industry, and length, then the letter rebuilds live as you type.

faq.q: How does the Job Description Matcher work?
faq.a: Paste the job description and it extracts the top 15 keywords by frequency (ignoring common stop-words) and marks each green if it already appears in your letter or red if it's missing. Clicking a keyword adds it to your skills field. It's a prompt to cover the role's language, not an automatic rewrite.

faq.q: Does it keep my letter to one page?
faq.a: It tracks the body word count and warns you: over 250 words when you've chosen 'concise', or over 400 words generally (with a reminder that cover letters should stay under one page), and it flags letters under 80 words as too short. You pick concise, standard or detailed length, and the generator adds or trims a paragraph accordingly.

faq.q: Can I save drafts and export?
faq.a: Yes. Save multiple named drafts in your browser and reload or delete them. There are three preview templates (Classic serif, Modern, Compact). Output is Copy Text, download as .txt, or Print/PDF via the browser. There are also clickable paragraph suggestions (opening hooks, why-this-company, STAR achievement framing, skill mapping, closings) that fill in your company, position and skills.
